question: Does removing ordinary invested-month rebalancing reduce costs enough to improve the economics of the already selected low-unit allocation, while preserving every existing risk exit and entry constraint?

window.source: Only the exact Study29 saved new decoded fixture, to be bound by the root controller; no source reacquisition or field conversion.

single_policy_delta.first: Retain the original paused, pending-risk-exit and terminal decision guards.
single_policy_delta.while_invested: If any asset quantity is positive at an otherwise eligible completed month end, append skipped_passive_drift_while_invested with empty targets and orders. Do not create a rebalance plan.
single_policy_delta.when_flat: Otherwise delegate to the original month-end decision. This preserves initial flat attempts and ordinary month-end rebuilding after full risk liquidation and the original five complete flat days. Failed or zero-quantity initial entry may retry only at a subsequent normal month end, never daily.
single_policy_delta.partial_basket: Any positive leg suppresses ordinary top-ups of missing legs. Received dividends and CIL proceeds remain cash while invested.
single_policy_delta.no_extra_exception: The added predicate is inventory only; no new fee threshold, drift band, holding-period limit or price signal. Corporate-action transitions use the inherited ledger state.
single_policy_delta.entry_timing: Original D-close targets, D+1-open sells, D+3-close frozen independent buy budgets, D+4-open buys; no future-open resizing.
single_policy_delta.mandatory_exits: Original risk and terminal liquidation remain mandatory, subject to the unchanged quantity, capacity, execution and fee constraints.

unchanged: Whole shares; no borrowing; marked market exposure cannot exceed NAV.
Daily 2 percent loss, 40 percent drawdown, continuous peak, original risk event semantics and five complete flat-day recovery.
Frozen previous-20-completed-day conservative nominal capacity and all original budget, price and rounding rules.
T+3 modeled sale proceeds and dividend ex+45-day availability with 30 percent modeled withholding.
GLDM reverse split, event-open adverse CIL valuation and 45/90-day unavailable receivable; no duplicate fee.
Terminal open liquidation; separate settled cash, locked proceeds, dividend receivable and CIL receivable. No added post-terminal source.

saved_comparators.policy: Read saved summaries/ledgers only; no monthly or cash account rerun.

each_cost_scenario: No borrowing or illegal units; independent recorded-ledger verification passes.
mandatory_disclosure_not_a_winner_select: Primary and stress cash-plus-locked net profit changes relative to the same-cost saved monthly account.
Primary and stress total execution-cost, fill-count and observed drawdown changes.
Book CAGR, annual contribution, average market/cash exposure, zero legs, risk exit/re-entry and terminal settlement components.
No gain is inferred by merely adding back old costs; holdings and risk paths may change.
acceptance.no_search_or_rescue: One fixed comparison. Losing to monthly does not authorize changing a frequency, threshold, asset, fee or window.

interpretation.selection: Chosen after seeing Study29 fees and returns; the 2021-2025 history is seen, not an independent holdout.
interpretation.mechanism: A transaction-cost and weight-drift tradeoff for an investment allocation, not a new alpha claim. Drift can amplify winner concentration and risk as well as save fees.
interpretation.qualification: Passing supports only this conditional diagnostic. It does not change Study29, qualify a live strategy or change an existing deployment.
interpretation.cash_definition: Cash profit includes contracted but unsettled sale proceeds and excludes unpaid dividends/CIL and remaining inventory; it is not same-day withdrawable cash.
interpretation.fees: US broker fees, taxes and cash clocks remain explicit model scenarios, not verified user account terms.

root_must_bind_before_numeric_run: New implementation and exact inherited dependencies
